afterNames: FTS duplicate attacks G2-D002: three writes yield one hit in FTS, discover, archive and hybrid keyword search
additionalTests.evidence: Three writes leave one stored memory and exactly one ID in each of searchFts, discoverFts, public hybrid archive fallback and hybrid keyword results. Removing the INSERT-trigger replacement kills this case; restored application passes.

afterNames: FTS duplicate attacks G2-D002: opening a populated v5 database heals duplicate FTS rows once without losing memories
additionalTests.evidence: A raw native SQLite fixture contains three duplicate cobalt index rows and a separate quartz row. Opening via GnosysDB yields exactly one hit each and preserves both contents/schema version5. A second open leaves native data_version unchanged. Skipping repair and repeating repair each kill the case; both restored runs pass.

afterNames: FTS duplicate attacks ADV-FTS-001: reopening after external FTS loss keeps the existing memory searchable
additionalTests.evidence: Ordinary construction, insert and search succeed. After raw native DROP TABLE, LIKE fallback still finds the memory; reopen preserves content but search becomes empty. Ordinary failure reproduced on approved f4b9135; no temporary repair or successful feature-protection claim.

afterNames: routing reset attacks DEF-G1-001: reset clears several overrides and preserves every unrelated config value
additionalTests.evidence: Actual runRoutingSetup readline interaction reports reset success, but persisted old taskModels remain. Unrelated values including llm and dream remain byte-identical after canonical JSON serialization. Ordinary failure confirms the reset defect; source whitespace preservation is not claimed.

afterNames: routing reset attacks DEF-G1-001: reset then set one new override does not restore old routing or change unrelated config
additionalTests.evidence: Actual runRoutingSetup readline interaction reports reset success, but persisted old taskModels remain. Unrelated values including llm and dream remain byte-identical after canonical JSON serialization. Ordinary failure confirms the reset defect; source whitespace preservation is not claimed.

limitations: Archive search uses public hybridSearch semantic fallback over the central database. Standalone archive.db is outside this defect.
Routing preserves canonical serialized JSON values; raw source whitespace may change.
Open expected failures reproduce defects and do not establish successful feature protection.
